description:
The emulator smoke run (activity_tracker_portal-hfj, 2026-10-30, c069f06) found these gaps in docs/runbooks/device-smoke-delivery.md:

Step 3 cannot install as written (blocker). npm run build:android produces sender/app/android/app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug-unsigned.apk, not app-debug.apk: sender/app/plugins/with-pinned-android.cjs deliberately strips debug signing ('This enabling workspace produces unsigned development APKs only'). 5. Step 10: WorkManager reschedules the periodic job under a new JobScheduler id after each run (0, then 1). Rerun dumpsys before each forced run. Until gc5 is fixed, the background run's checkpoint waits behind the backlog and does not reach the report.

7. Optional: an emulator variant. Map the Mac's ts.net name to 10.0.2.2, because the emulator cannot reach the Mac's Tailscale IP. Run the proxy on 127.0.0.1:8765. Synthetic Health Connect data needs a writer app.

title: Sender crashes with a JNI global reference table overflow when the outbox is large
description:
Found in the emulator smoke run (activity_tracker_portal-hfj, 2026-10-30, smoke checkout c069f06, Pixel 10 Pro XL emulator, Android 16, debug dev build).

With about 1,000 messages queued in the Sender's outbox (grown by activity_tracker_portal-gc5), tapping Begin draining was followed about 7 s later by a native abort:
  JNI ERROR (app bug): global reference table overflow (max=51200)
  Summary: 50367 of java.nio.DirectByteBuffer
The aborting thread was in expo-sqlite: SQLiteModule.getAll -> NativeStatement.getTransformedColumnValues -> expo NativeArrayBuffer.initHybrid. expo-sqlite returns each BLOB column value as a native ArrayBuffer that holds a JNI global reference until JavaScript garbage-collects it. The Sender's status and refresh paths read the whole outbox, including sealed BLOBs (activity_tracker_portal-mfv), after every Sync and on every foreground, so the live references grow with queue size times read frequency.

Consequences: once the outbox is large, the app can crash on ordinary screen refreshes, and every relaunch repeats the same reads. A phone that is offline for a while, or any build affected by gc5, reaches this state.

Fix direction: status and enrollment reads must not fetch BLOB columns for the whole outbox (mfv), and any read that must return BLOBs should be bounded (LIMIT, or count/aggregate queries). Consider a test that pins the number of BLOB values a status read returns.
acceptance_criteria: Status, refresh and enrollment reads return no outbox BLOB values, or a bounded number, and a Sender with several thousand queued messages survives repeated refreshes on a device.
notes:
Reproduced twice: with 1,008 and then 1,052 queued messages, tapping Begin draining crashed the app both times, and sender_enrollment.phase stayed 'enrolled'. The installation can therefore never start draining. Cause: beginDrain runs statusFrom inside its transaction (manage-sender-enrollment.ts:433-441), and statusFrom (:310-333) loads every outbox message with outboxMessages(handle) only to check the acknowledgement and emptiness. The post-action screen refresh calls status() and does it again.
Third crash, possibly related: the process started at 12:23:29, when the outbox still held 1,052 messages; it ran the reset and installation 2's enrollment, then died at 12:24:59 during installation 2's first Sync (its outbox under 200 messages) with SIGSEGV (null pointer dereference, fault addr 0x14) in libhermesvm.so on the mqt_v_js thread, called from facebook::react::RuntimeScheduler. Symbols are stripped, so the link to the leaked ArrayBuffers is unproven.

title: Idle Sync runs stage more messages than one delivery pass sends, so the outbox never catches up
description:
Found in the emulator smoke run (activity_tracker_portal-hfj, 2026-10-30, smoke checkout c069f06, Pixel 10 Pro XL emulator, Android 16).

With all 41 projected types advertised and no Health Connect changes, every Sync run stages 83 outbox messages: one empty change-cycle ingest batch and one change completion per type, plus the run's Sync Checkpoint. The Sender's run_checkpoints sit at sequences 166, 249 and 332, exactly 83 apart. A delivery pass sends at most MAX_DELIVERY_ATTEMPTS = 64 messages (sender/app/src/shell/compose-sender.ts:31, loop at :240) and then stops until another trigger. After three runs (foreground, foreground, manual) the Portal held sequences 1-193 and the Sender still queued 139 (194-332).

Consequences:
- The queue grows by about 19 messages per idle run, foreground or background, without bound until storage admission stops it.
- An idle Sync costs 83 HTTP round trips; over Tailscale on a phone that is many seconds per run, and it eats into the 480 s background budget.
- The device smoke runbook's step 7.4 ('repeat Sync now until a tap delivers only one new outbox message') can never be met.

The runbook's ingest numbers otherwise looked right: all 64 synthetic records arrived in the initial snapshot (steps 45 including 15 older than 30 days, weight 9, heart rate 10), gaps 0.

Fix direction needs a governed decision (coordinate-sender-sync / shell delivery loop / change-cycle staging): either stop staging empty change batches and completions for types with no changes, or let a run keep delivering within its deadline until the outbox drains, or both.
acceptance_criteria: An idle Sync run with no Health Connect changes leaves the outbox drained (only its checkpoint delivered), and a test pins that staging per idle run never exceeds what one run delivers.
notes: Operator decision 2026-10-30: fix both parts. (1) Enabling shell change: after a Polling Run, keep delivering passes until the Outbox drains or the deadline nears, sequenced after the 636/mfv fix so extra passes do not repeat whole-Outbox reads. (2) Governed change: a change cycle whose read finds no changes advances the saved changes token on the Sender without staging an Ingest Batch or Change Completion; the Sync Checkpoint's per-type no-change outcome remains the Portal's polling signal. Needs Gate A drafts for stage-outbox-batch and coordinate-sender-sync successors.

title: Deliver coordinate-sender-sync@2: absolute deadlines for background triggers
description:
Governed successor of coordinate-sender-sync@1 (Operator decision 2026-10-16, PR #41 / 2rv.9).

The problem: coordinate-sender-sync@1 starts a run's relative budget only after recovery, when the run opens (coordinate-sender-sync.ts startMono), and R8 merges triggers with no budget if any merged trigger had none, and otherwise the latest budget. A background callback from schedule-background-polling@1, with an 8-minute window, can therefore overrun:
- when it queues behind an active run;
- when recovery and observation take time;
- when it merges with an unbudgeted foreground or manual trigger.

The approver's review of PR #41 found that the shell cannot fix this without breaking R8 coalescing (round 2 objection 2) or recording deadline stops as read-failed instead of the R10 time-budget-reached outcomes (round 2 objection 1).

Likely scope:
- TriggerRequest gains an absolute monotonic deadline.
- A merged follow-up honours the earliest live background deadline, without shortening the active run (R8).
- A caller whose deadline passes before its run opens resolves without new work.

title: Observe Operator conditions from the Expo shell
description:
Enabling task. notify-operator-conditions@1 leaves wiring to the Sender shell. The shell must:
- create one OperatorConditions instance per process over the opened database and the Expo notification adapter (pv2.3);
- call observe after every Polling Run with its RunSummary, and at app start, at foreground return, and after each enrollment change with the current EnrollmentStatus and the installation key status;
- show conditions() on the status screen (2rv.8).

The approver's implementation review of PR #40 (2026-10-16) left three integration responsibilities unpinned by the pack:
1. Instance ownership. Observations serialize only within one instance, so the foreground and background entry points must share one instance or coordinate. Otherwise two instances can both notify the same unacknowledged onset.
2. Notifier completion. observe awaits the notifier without a deadline, so a pending notifier stalls that instance's observation queue. The notification adapter must complete or fail within a bounded time.
3. Observation freshness. Queued observations carry no installation-generation or run-sequence guard, so the shell must not submit a stale observation after a reset, an unlink, or a newer observation.
Carries no governed behaviour.

title: Qualify cold-start background runs with an embedded-bundle Sender build
description: From GPT 6 Astra's PR #47 review (2026-10-17). The development build loads JavaScript from Metro, but the pinned expo-modules-core RNHeadlessAppLoader starts the app's ReactHost without the development launcher's server URL, which the launcher holds in memory only. So in a development build, a background run that has to start the app from scratch after Android killed its process may fail to load any JavaScript. kv7's runbook therefore exercises only background runs while the process is alive. ADR 0036's background qualification (callback delivery, interruption and restart recovery) needs a build with the JavaScript embedded: a release variant, or debugOptimized if it embeds the bundle, signed for private installation. The release network config already allows the ts.net Portal. Add the build script and the runbook steps, and run a cold-start background check: kill the backgrounded process with adb shell am kill org.activitytracker.sender (not force-stop, which cancels scheduled jobs until the app is reopened), then force or wait for the job, and confirm a background Sync Checkpoint arrives.
notes:
From Astra's PR #47 round 2 (non-blocking): when revising runbook step 3 and step 10, replace 'keeps Metro's address in memory only' with 'The background loader does not restore the Metro server configuration selected through the launcher' (DevLauncherRecentlyOpenedAppsRegistry.kt persists recently opened URLs; the active dev-server configuration is in memory and RNHeadlessAppLoader does not restore it).
2026-10-30 emulator smoke run (hfj, Pixel 10 Pro XL emulator, Android 16, debug dev build from c069f06): a warm background run (app at home, process alive, forced job) delivered 64 messages. After 'am kill' (jobs kept), forcing the rescheduled WorkManager job restarted the process but delivered nothing within 60 s, and Metro saw no bundle request. Logcat showed React Native dev support trying ws://10.0.2.2:8081 (the emulator default host, not the launcher's Metro URL) and failing with 'Software caused connection abort'. Note: WorkManager reschedules the periodic job under a new JobScheduler id after every run (0, then 1), so 'cmd jobscheduler run -f' needs a fresh dumpsys each time.

title: manage-sender-enrollment status() materializes the whole Outbox
description:
Found by the Codex review of PR #41 (2rv.9), 2026-10-16. manage-sender-enrollment@1's status() derives its answer from outboxMessages(handle) (manage-sender-enrollment.ts ~325). That runs SELECT * FROM outbox_messages and returns every sealed BLOB, then filters by installation. The shell now reads status once per delivery pass and once per source-call step. Even one call reads and allocates the entire Outbox, which can approach the supported 512 MiB, so a single status read can exhaust a background window or memory on a large Initial Snapshot backlog.

title: Reread conditions after the status observation on the Sender screen
description: From GPT 6 Astra's PR #45 (2rv.8) round 2 review at 188357f, non-blocking. use-sender-screen.ts refresh() reads shell.status() and shell.conditions() in parallel. status() runs through enrollmentAction, whose finally awaits operator.observe(), so conditions() can finish before that observation updates operator_conditions, and one refresh can show an older condition list until the next refresh. title: Bound control-message sizes in the Wire Protocol
description: The Codex review of PR #38 (2rv.4) found that the advertised max_message_bytes binds only Ingest Batches: accept-ingest-batch enforces it, while stage-sync-checkpoint can stage, and accept-sync-checkpoint accepts, a Sync Checkpoint of any size, and the protocol bounds no record_types count. The Portal's Outbox route therefore keeps a 1 MiB floor (DELIVERY_BODY_FLOOR) on its transport ceiling, so control messages above the batch limit still reach their units. A control message above that floor would get an empty 413 and stall the Sender's Outbox. A later protocol or unit version should bound control-message sizes, for example by bounding record_types to the advertised projection schemas, so that the transport ceiling can rest on a protocol guarantee.
acceptance_criteria: Control-message sizes are bounded by a published protocol or unit rule, or the Operator decides the 1 MiB floor suffices.

title: Add a metadata-only archived identity read to the Operational Store
description: Found by GPT 6 Astra in the accept-sync-completion@1 implementation review (PR #32). Every accept-* unit (accept-ingest-batch@1, accept-capability-acknowledgement@1, accept-sync-completion@1) checks a delivered message's identity with StoreView.archived_message, the only per-sequence read in operational-store@2. For a sequence held by an Ingest Batch that read also loads the batch's items (projections and retracted identities) through archived_items, so a sequence-content-mismatch answer reads one archived message's health data it does not need. The read is bounded (one message, at most max_record_count items), read-only, and returned to no caller, and no frozen requirement forbids it: accept-sync-completion@1's no-item-data rule covers only its completion proof (R7). A later Operational Store version could add an identity-only read (message SHA-256 and receipt), and the accept-* units could adopt it in their next versions.
acceptance_criteria: A published Operational Store version offers an identity-only per-sequence read, and the accept-* units' identity checks no longer load item data.

title: Harden the coordinate-sender-sync acceptance pack against four non-discriminating gaps

title: Harden published Sender suites' contents() to whole-database snapshots
description:
GPT 6 Astra's Gate B review of stage-sync-checkpoint@1 (2026-10-14) found that its contents() helper compared only selected columns of three tables. A mutant that created an extra table and wrote to it before returning staging-conflict passed every test, and so did a migration that added an extra table. The checkpoint suite was corrected before freeze to snapshot every schema object and every row of every table, and to compare the whole schema across its migration.

The published suites use the same narrow pattern: stage-outbox-batch@1, stage-sync-completion@1, begin-reconciliation-snapshot@1, and begin-initial-snapshot@2. Their implementations are correct (each was reviewed), but their 'writes nothing' and migration assertions would not catch an extra table or an unrelated write. Harden them in their next pack versions. See also 2ov.
